bayts.text: Praise be to Him who sends down frailty and disease, and who sends down healing and remedy,
He who commanded the servants to supplicate (duʿāʾ), so that by it they may ward off affliction.
Then upon him who, whenever he touched one who was sick, that one recovered without delay and obtained what he sought:
Muḥammad, our wise physician; upon him be the purest greetings of peace of our Generous Lord,
and upon his Family and Companions, possessors of eminence, so long as the sick have need of healing.
That said, I am today afflicted with pains, seeking the help of Him who answers the one who calls,
and to Him I complain of the harm that has touched me, until I see myself as one at death's door.
O our Lord, O our Lord, O our Lord! O our Lord, O our Lord, ward off our harm!
By the standing of the Best of the worlds, the Most Noble, and then by the blessing of the great month of Ramaḍān.
O God, O Compassionate, O Merciful! O Kind, O Generous, O Immense!
Forgive our sins, accept from us, protect our sanctuary, and pass over our faults.
And send down, O our Lord, the best of blessings in place of the evil of the punishments we fear.
And grant us good manners and excellences, and restrain from us afflictions and calamities.
And grant us eagerness for acts of obedience, and restrain from us laziness at all times.
O Kind, O Gentle (Laṭīf), O Giver of well-being! O You in whose hand is the command of creation, O Healer (Shāfī)!
Send down Your healing in place of the disease, and do not treat us with trial.
And send down benefit in place of harm, and send down good in place of evil.
And send down knowledge in place of ignorance, and send down generosity in place of miserliness.
And send down sufficiency in place of poverty, and send down gratitude in place of ingratitude.
And heal all the Muslims swiftly, then guard them against fear and sorrow in time to come.
And deliver them, and grant them well-being, and be gentle with them, and do not take them to account for the multitude of their sins.
For indeed, though they have disobeyed You, O One, out of heedlessness, they have not associated anyone with You.
And indeed their bodies are never able to bear Your trials, because of a weakness that is manifest.
Their hearts never incline to any besides You, from here until tomorrow;
but rather the stealthy slipping of the limbs has led them to the ugliest of ugly deeds.
So do not take them to account for what does not diminish You, and grant them that which does not profit You.
O God, O Turner of hearts! Turn our hearts away from faults.
And inspire us with love of every Muslim, and deliver us from the evil of every wrongdoer.
And make all the Muslims, altogether, friends to us, so that we are spared harm.
And keep all the believing men and believing women upon guidance, and then grant them well-being tomorrow.
And make all the Muslim men and Muslim women to rise, in the increase of their God-fearing piety (Taqwā).
And make all the learned practise what they know, and make all who practise sincere.
And make all the sincere ascetic, and make all the ascetics givers of sincere counsel.
And make all the givers of counsel truthful, and make all the truthful triumphant.
And inspire us, O our Lord, with service to the Muslims always, and with mercy.
And place in us for them guidance and good, and restrain from them harm and injury from us.
And inspire us with love of them for Your Face, and inspire them with love of us, so that we may walk the path.
And place all my brothers and my kinsfolk in mercy on the day when toil becomes severe.
And grant us, here and there, a portion, a cause for envy, by Your favour, so that we may be favoured.
And grant us the noble traits of character, together with mutual love without discord.
And make our young honour the elder, and make our elder help the young.
And make our hearts united in mutual affection, without quarrelling and without envy,
and without disputing and without turning the back on one another, and without mutual hatred and without aversion,
until we become Muslims who are humble, and believers who are sincere and righteous.
And forgive us, and grant us well-being with a well-being that in the two abodes will not fade.
And protect, and surround, and restrain us from any wrongdoing, and deliver every Muslim man and Muslim woman.
And grant us, O our Lord, a good ending (Ḥusn al-Khitām), at the time of death and tomorrow on the Day of Resurrection,
by the standing of the best of those who healed the diseases and bestowed what is desired and sought:
Muḥammad, our noble physician, who cures diseases and illnesses.
And send blessings upon him, and then peace, and upon his Family with the noble Companions,
so long as the one occupied with supplication prospers, and the sick is restored to health by seeking healing.
And for the composer also: may God increase him in healing and abundance.
O you who seek to ward off every disease, do not depart from the seeking of healing (Maṭlab ash-Shifāʾ),
and persevere in it in the evening and the morning, and be sincere: you will attain healing and success,
by the permission of our Lord and the standing of the Chosen One (Al-Muṣṭafā); may our Lord bless him as He chose him.
